Disaster decision desk · exercise prototype

IndTrana

IndTrana is a decision desk for disaster agencies: it gathers evidence, shows how fresh and how certain it is, and makes sure two different accountable officers approve a proposal before anything is handed to the official alerting authority.

Exercise prototype — synthetic data — not a live warning system

The six-step alert path. Choose a step to see what software does, what a person decides and where IndTrana stops.

1. Sense

Software assists

Collects synthetic feeds, shows how old each one is, holds bad records in quarantine.

A person decides

Reads source freshness and decides which evidence to trust.

Where IndTrana stops

No live agency feed is connected.

2. Predict

Software assists

Rule-based triggers flag cases. Rehearsal estimates carry ranges and citations. Abstains when evidence is thin.

A person decides

Reviews each flagged case and its cited evidence.

Where IndTrana stops

Figures are rehearsal figures, never accuracy.

3. Decide

Software assists

Attaches a cited review brief to the draft.

A person decides

A maker drafts and submits. A different checker approves or rejects, with a written reason.

Where IndTrana stops

Software cannot approve. One person cannot do both.

4. Hand over

Software assists

After approval, prepares a private Draft CAP file and department tasks.

A person decides

An officer hands the approved draft to the alerting authority.

Where IndTrana stops

IndTrana has no way to send a public warning.

5. Reach

Software assists

Rehearsal only: department desks and teams answer inside the app.

A person decides

Desks acknowledge tasks and request teams. Team members answer.

Where IndTrana stops

Phones are reached by the authority's own system. Nobody is called or texted.

6. Learn

Software assists

Counts hits, misses and false alarms. Proposes a threshold change as a statistics-only difference.

A person decides

A maker proposes, a different checker reviews, only an administrator applies.

Where IndTrana stops

Approval alone never changes the engine.

What it is

A decision-support workbench for emergency operations centres. It gathers hazard evidence, shows how fresh it is, and drafts cited response proposals.

Who it is for

Operations centres, department desks and response teams of a disaster-management agency, and the people who audit them.

What it does

Routes every proposal through an independent two-person approval, produces a private draft alert file and scripted tasks, and records each step in an audit trail.

What it does not do

It sends no public warning, dispatches no team and contacts no outside agency. Its data is synthetic.

Status. A local synthetic demonstration prototype for rehearsal, version 0.3.0, 14 November 2026. It has no government approval or certification. Security testing so far is a developer self-assessment, not an independent audit. Rehearsal statistics are not forecasting accuracy.

What is asked of the reader. Judge whether the method (cited evidence, two accountable people, a full record) is worth carrying forward. See Deployment for what a government deployment would still need.

A note on names: the product was renamed from AEGIS to IndTrana on 13 November 2026. Technical identifiers keep the older prefix on purpose so that installs, sign-in and the database keep working, for example aegis_roles, AEGIS_* and the project name ai-project-aegis.

Alert path

From signal to learning, with people in charge

In disaster response a wrong or late warning costs trust and can cost lives. Accountability must sit with named people, not a model.

The path has six steps. The boundary that matters most lies between Hand over and Reach: IndTrana prepares a draft, and a person gives it to the official alerting authority, whose own system reaches telephones.

How a proposal moves

Step through the life cycle. Each step shows the role that performs it and what is recorded.

1. Draft Maker

The maker saves a proposal for a case. A cited review brief is captured with it as an immutable snapshot.

Recorded: Proposal, snapshot, audit event.

2. Submitted Maker

The maker submits it for independent review. An opted-in checker may receive a fixed-text email notice.

Recorded: Status change and audit event, in one transaction.

3. Approved or rejected Checker

A different checker reads the cited evidence and decides, with a written reason. Rejection ends the proposal. Approval allows a private Draft CAP file and tasks.

Recorded: Approval row and audit event. A database trigger refuses a checker who is the maker.

4. Tasks prepared Maker

The maker prepares scripted tasks for three desks: control room, infrastructure and communications.

Recorded: A versioned task receipt and audit events.

5. Task acknowledged Department desk

Each desk sees only its own task and acknowledges it with a short reason.

Recorded: Task state and an audit event marked with department authority.

6. Team requested Department desk

On an acknowledged task the desk requests one invented team, after reading why it is suggested. The team answers on its My Team page.

Recorded: Request and report rows, a fixed-template timeline line marked SIMULATION, an audit event. Nobody is contacted.

7. Team completed Response team

The team moves through accepted, en route, on site and completed. It may send a situation report or ask for support. The desk can record an answer on its behalf or stand it down.

Recorded: Append-only reports and timeline lines. Notes never reach the timeline.

8. Task closed Department desk

Only when no team request is active can the desk close its task with a reason.

Recorded: Task closure and audit event.

Step 1 of 8

All use cases

UC-01 Sign in
Actor
Any person with an account at the agency identity provider
Goal
Obtain a verified session with the correct agency and role.
Preconditions
An account exists at the identity provider, with an agency and at least one role assigned there.
Main steps
  1. Open the site and choose Sign in, then Continue to sign in.
  2. Enter user name, password and second factor on the identity provider's own page.
  3. Return to IndTrana, which checks the provider's signature and opens a 15-minute session.
What is recorded
A sealed session cookie in the browser. The provider keeps its own sign-in log. IndTrana stores no password.
What never happens
IndTrana never sees a password. Role and agency are never taken from the browser. There is no sign-in without the provider.
UC-02 Watch sources and their freshness
Actor
Any signed-in role
Goal
Know which data feeds are late, missing or odd before relying on them.
Preconditions
Signed in as a member of the exercise agency.
Main steps
  1. Open Source Freshness and filter by state.
  2. Open a feed to see its recent history.
  3. Open DataFusion Replay to see what was accepted, repeated or quarantined.
What is recorded
Nothing is written; these pages are read-only.
What never happens
It never contacts a real agency feed. Agreement between feeds is not proof that they are right. Quarantined records are never released from this page.
UC-03 Review an incident
Actor
Maker (any reader role may read)
Goal
Understand one exercise case: evidence, readiness, unknowns and any team response.
Preconditions
A synthetic incident exists in the agency.
Main steps
  1. Search, sort and filter the Incident Registry.
  2. Open a case; read its evidence, the readiness checks and the explicit unknowns.
  3. Use the spatial explorer (1, 3 or 5 km) to see nearby candidate sources; read the Team response panel and timeline.
What is recorded
Nothing is written.
What never happens
It never creates or changes a case. It never computes a real flood-risk score. Nearby is a candidate, never proof of cause.
UC-04 Draft a proposal
Actor
Maker
Goal
Prepare a cited proposal (for example a warning draft) for independent review.
Preconditions
A case in the maker's agency; the maker holds the incident_operator role.
Main steps
  1. Open the Approval Workbench and choose the incident and the action type.
  2. Write the rationale. Save the draft; the cited review brief is captured with it.
  3. Optionally run a bounded assistance run (fixed step budget, stops before submission) and simulate.
  4. Submit for independent review.
What is recorded
The proposal with an immutable snapshot of the evidence and citations, and audit events written in the same transaction. An opted-in checker may get a fixed-text email notice.
What never happens
It never sends anything. The maker cannot approve. Text typed by a client is never accepted as model output.
UC-05 Independent approval or rejection
Actor
Checker
Goal
Decide, with a written reason, on a proposal drafted by someone else.
Preconditions
A submitted proposal whose maker is a different person.
Main steps
  1. Open the Approval Workbench and the submitted proposal.
  2. Read the cited evidence and rationale.
  3. Write a reason and approve or reject.
What is recorded
An approval row (checker, decision, reason, time) and an audit event, in one transaction.
What never happens
Self-approval is refused by the API and by a database trigger. Approval sends no warning: it only allows a private Draft CAP file and department tasks.
UC-06 Department acknowledges and closes tasks
Actor
Department desk
Goal
Work the approved tasks of one department.
Preconditions
An approved proposal whose scripted tasks the maker has prepared. The desk's account carries a department claim.
Main steps
  1. Open the Department Inbox; it lists only this department's tasks.
  2. Acknowledge a task with a short reason.
  3. When no team request is active, close the task with a reason.
What is recorded
Task state changes and audit events marked with department authority.
What never happens
It never shows another department's tasks. Time targets are rehearsal targets, not contractual. Closing is refused while a team request is active.
UC-07 A desk requests a team and the team responds
Actor
Department desk and Response team
Goal
Rehearse the last step of the chain inside the app.
Preconditions
An acknowledged task on an approved proposal; invented teams exist in the fixture.
Main steps
  1. The desk opens Request a team and reads why each team is suggested (matching capability, free capacity, availability, estimated travel time).
  2. The desk requests one team.
  3. On a phone-sized view the team sees the request on My Team and presses Accept, I am en route, I am on site, Completed; it may send a situation report or ask for support.
  4. The desk can record an answer on a team's behalf, stand the team down or mark a support flag handled.
What is recorded
Request and report rows, fixed-template timeline lines starting with SIMULATION, and audit events.
What never happens
Nobody is called, texted, emailed or radioed. Software never creates a request. Notes never reach the timeline. Teams are invented, not real units.
UC-08 Shift handover
Actor
Maker, checker, auditor or administrator
Goal
Brief the next shift on what changed.
Preconditions
Signed in with a reading role.
Main steps
  1. Open Shift Handover and choose a window of 1 to 72 hours.
  2. Read the brief; each line cites record identifiers.
  3. Download or print it.
What is recorded
Nothing is written or saved.
What never happens
It is not a forecast, an approval or a dispatch. Reasons, rationales and proposal bodies are never copied into it.
UC-09 Ask the operator copilot
Actor
Maker, checker, auditor or administrator
Goal
Get a quick, cited answer about the agency's records.
Preconditions
Signed in with a reading role.
Main steps
  1. Type a question of 3 to 300 characters or pick an example.
  2. The question is mapped to one fixed intent, or the copilot abstains.
  3. Read the answer and the records it cites.
What is recorded
Nothing is written.
What never happens
It cannot act, approve, notify or forecast, and it ignores instructions typed into a question. Unknown questions abstain.
UC-10 Run a drill
Actor
Maker starts; maker and checker respond
Goal
Practise the chain on a simulated clock.
Preconditions
The proactive watch is on and not paused.
Main steps
  1. The maker starts a drill from a fixed scenario.
  2. The clock moves only when someone advances it.
  3. Makers and checkers respond to the injected evidence; the coach report compares elapsed minutes with rehearsal targets.
What is recorded
Drill state and drill audit rows. Injected evidence lives only inside the drill.
What never happens
No real record, proposal, task or message is created. The kill switch blocks new drill writes. Scores are rehearsal targets, not contractual.
UC-11 Post-event learning and a threshold proposal
Actor
Maker, a different checker or administrator, and an administrator
Goal
Compare earlier triggers with what happened and propose a change to a threshold.
Preconditions
A closed event window.
Main steps
  1. The maker closes or replays a window and reads the statistics, labelled by basis.
  2. The maker proposes a threshold change; a different checker or administrator reviews it.
  3. Only an administrator can apply an approved change, creating a new versioned overlay.
What is recorded
Windows, proposals, versioned configuration and a learning audit.
What never happens
The statistics are never accuracy. Approval alone never changes the engine. Applying is blocked while the kill switch is engaged.
UC-12 Administer connectors and the kill switch
Actor
Administrator of the exercise agency
Goal
Set up optional data sources and stop automation at once if needed.
Preconditions
The proactive overlay is on and a connector key is set.
Main steps
  1. Open Administration, Connectors; enter keys (write-only) and test them.
  2. Switch a connector on; for email, also needs the host switch.
  3. Engage or release the kill switch.
What is recorded
Connector audit and pause audit rows.
What never happens
A saved secret is never shown again. A test sends no message. SMS, WhatsApp and authority notification cannot be enabled.

Actor
Any signed-in role

Learn the screen quickly, with steps matching the signed-in role.

Main steps

Any signed-in role

  2. Read the notes for each version, newest first, grouped as New, Improved, Fixed and Security. The repository also keeps a CHANGELOG.md in developer wording.

What never happens
It changes no record. 0.3.0 is the first tagged release; the 0.2.0 and 0.1.0 entries are summaries of earlier work with a period instead of a date.

Architecture

How it is built

System context

Six kinds of people use IndTrana through a browser. The organisation's identity provider signs them in. Public reference data and an email provider are optional and off by default. Public warning channels and outside agencies are not connected, because IndTrana has no code that sends to them.

Runtime architecture

One host, one Docker Compose project. The web application is the browser's server layer: it holds the session and forwards the person's token to the API. The API alone reaches the database, which publishes no host port. Web, API and the sign-in front door listen on the loopback address only. Click a component in the picture, or switch optional overlays on and off. With all overlays off you see the base system.

Select web, api, db or the identity provider in the picture (keyboard: Tab, then Enter).

Web application (Next.js, port 3000)

What it does. Serves the pages and acts as the browser's server layer. It runs the sign-in flow, seals the session, checks the origin of every write, filters fields and forwards the person's token to the API.

What it trusts. It trusts nothing from the browser: every request is checked for a valid session, the right role and the right agency.

Controls that apply

  • Sign-in gate on every page and route
  • Sealed A256GCM session cookie, 15 minutes
  • Origin check on all state-changing handlers
  • Nonce-based page security policy
  • Relay with fixed hosts and no redirects

API service (FastAPI, port 8000)

What it does. Holds the rules: role lists per route, agency scope, maker-checker, assessment, spatial checks, CAP draft export.

What it trusts. It trusts only a correctly signed token from the configured provider; agency and role come only from that token.

Controls that apply

  • RS256 signature, issuer, audience, expiry
  • Explicit role list per route (inventory test)
  • Other agency gets 403
  • Unknown fields refused
  • no-store and nosniff on replies

Database (PostgreSQL with PostGIS)

What it does. Stores incidents, proposals, approvals, audit and the other tables of Figure 7.

What it trusts. It is reachable only by the API inside the Compose network; no host port is published.

Controls that apply

  • Transactions and row locks
  • Trigger against self-approval
  • One approval per proposal
  • Audit written in the same transaction
  • Row-level security: not yet built

Identity provider (local Keycloak and TLS front door)

What it does. Signs people in and issues signed tokens carrying agency, role and, where relevant, department or team.

What it trusts. It is owned by the agency. In the demo it is a local stand-in in development mode.

Controls that apply

  • Passwords and second factor live here only
  • Roles assigned by administrators at the provider
  • Open finding M3 for the development-mode console
  • Local demo accounts only

Sign-in and request flow

Sign-in uses the OIDC authorization-code flow with PKCE. The person types the password only at the identity provider. Step through the eleven steps.

All steps
  1. Press Continue to sign in. The web application creates state, nonce and a PKCE challenge and keeps them in a sealed flow cookie.
  2. The browser follows the redirect to the identity provider, carrying the challenge, state and nonce.
  3. The person enters password and second factor on the provider's page. IndTrana never sees them.
  4. The browser returns to the web application with a one-time code and the state value.
  5. The web application exchanges the code and the PKCE verifier with the provider, server to server.
  6. It checks state and nonce and seals the session in an HttpOnly cookie that lasts 15 minutes. The token stays on the server.
  7. On a later request the browser sends the cookie; writes also carry an Origin header.
  8. The web application checks origin, role and fields, then forwards the bearer token from the session to the API.
  9. The API verifies signature, issuer, audience and expiry, takes agency and role from the signed claims and checks the route's role list.
  10. One transaction: lock the row, check the agency, write the change and its audit record.
  11. The reply travels back with no-store and nosniff headers, through the web application, to the browser.

Logical data model

Proposals, approvals and audit sit at the centre. The department tasks of a proposal are kept as a versioned receipt inside the proposal record and its audit. Public intake is isolated and never links to cases. Connector secrets are stored encrypted.

Security

Who is trusted with what

  • Identity. Only signed RS256 tokens from the configured identity provider are accepted. Agency and role come only from the signed token; the browser can never supply them.
  • Maker-checker. The checker must be a different person. The API and a database trigger both refuse self-approval; one approval per proposal; decision and audit commit together.
  • Sign-in gate. Every page and route except the landing and sign-in pages needs a valid 15-minute sealed session. Other agencies' records are refused.
  • Browser protections. Nonce-based page security policy, frames refused, origin check on every state-changing handler, and a relay with fixed hosts so the browser contacts no third-party host.
  • Limits on automation. Bounded, draft-only runs; read-only copilot that abstains when unsure; display-only public data; one fixed-text email channel to opted-in staff.

What the 14 November 2026 test did and found

A developer self-assessment by the development assistant on the signed-in product with eight local demo accounts. It is not an independent penetration test and does not replace the audit that government hosting requires. Two live agencies were not tested.

No critical or high finding. Two code reviews, about 200 scripted requests as each demo role, npm audit and pip-audit with no known vulnerability, and a secret scan with none found. Three medium findings (two fixed, one open) and eight low (five fixed, three known limits).

Findings of the 14 November 2026 developer test
IdSeverityFindingStatus
M1MediumOne web route that computes a synthetic index had no same-origin checkFixed and re-tested; a test now lists every state-changing handler
M2MediumPlatform-wide administration accepted an administrator from any agencyFixed and re-tested; limited to the exercise agency's administrator
M3MediumLocal sign-in provider runs in development mode with its console behind the same front doorOpen: deployment prerequisite (harmless on the laptop; port is 127.0.0.1 only)
L1LowThree public-feed values shown without escaping on one cardFixed and tested
L2LowAPI replies carried no defensive headersFixed: nosniff on every reply, no-store unless the route sets its own
L3LowRisk input ignored unknown fields; NaN or Infinity caused a server errorFixed: unknown fields refused, non-finite numbers get 422
L4LowConnector updates had no key-count limit and echoed unknown key namesFixed: at most 32 keys; echo only plain identifiers
L5LowA NUL character in a rationale caused a server errorFixed: validation reply and a plain sentence on the page
L6LowA copied session cookie works until expiry (at most 15 minutes) after sign-outKnown limit: needs a server-side session list
L7LowProvider admin password passed as an argument inside the container by scriptsKnown limit, local only
L8LowFallback database password, partial container hardening, no per-session relay limitKnown limit: to be closed in hosting work

Not done: two live agencies, a sign-in brute-force run, load and denial-of-service tests, a container image scan, an independent tester, Linux and macOS.

Walkthrough

The application, page by page

Screenshots were captured on 14 November 2026 from the running application. All data is synthetic. Use the buttons, the list or the left and right arrow keys. Select a screenshot to enlarge it.

Sensor link and patent

Keeping sensor readings flowing: a rehearsal

Indian Patent No. 598835 (Application No. 201741007139, filed 28 February 2017, granted 12 August 2026) is titled “Dynamic Bandwidth System for IoT Networks via Satellite and Internet Infrastructure”. The patentee is Bharath Bejjarapu, a co-owner of IndTrana. It is described here from its title and from a public listing of the publication notice, which was not verified against the Patent Office record; the full specification has not been reviewed. IndTrana itself is not described as patented, and nothing here states what the patent's claims cover.

The Resilient Sensor Link page is a browser-only rehearsal simulation. Step through the storm timeline.

1. 72 hours before landfall

Ground internet laneup
Satellite laneup

All links up; every sensor reports.

2. 12 hours before landfall

Ground internet lanereduced
Satellite laneup

Rain bands arrive and towers start to fail; ground capacity is reduced and the lowest-priority feeds start to wait.

3. Landfall

Ground internet lanecut
Satellite laneup

Ground network cut; life-safety gauges keep reporting over satellite, and lower-priority feeds wait.

4. Peak

Ground internet lanecut
Satellite lanereduced

Satellite capacity is reduced; life-safety gauges are served first and lower-priority feeds wait.

5. Recovery

Ground internet laneup
Satellite laneup

Ground links return; held feeds catch up.

Moment 1 of 5

Nothing is transmitted, no satellite or radio link is used and nothing is stored. Values are synthetic, and the priority classes and switch-over rules are IndTrana's own rehearsal choices.

A field deployment would still need:

  • Sensor gateways able to use both link types
  • Satellite terminals and licensed capacity from an authorised provider
  • A bandwidth policy agreed with the agency
  • Security review of the links
  • Testing against real outages
  • Review of the patent specification by its owner

How IndTrana reaches people

Public warnings never go through IndTrana. On 12 November 2026 the owner lifted the no-dispatch rule for one thing only: email notices to IndTrana's own signed-in staff who opted in, using fixed templates with no case content, behind two switches that are off by default.

Deployment

Today, and what is not yet built

Today IndTrana runs as exactly one Docker Compose project on one computer. Windows is the tested system; Linux and macOS start paths are written but have not been run there. The list below is taken from the project's readiness document of 11 November 2026, written from secondary sources; every clause must be confirmed against the official text. It is not legal or compliance advice. IndTrana is not ready for government production use.

Status and limits

What is and is not ready

  • IndTrana is a local synthetic demonstration prototype for rehearsal. It is not a live warning system.
  • It sends no public warning, dispatches no team and contacts no outside agency. The only message it can send is a fixed-text email notice to its own signed-in staff who opted in, and only when two switches are on (off by default).
  • All data is synthetic exercise data. Public reference feeds (Earth Watch, Live Earth) are optional, display-only and never create cases, proposals or alerts.
  • Rehearsal statistics and the synthetic model scores are not forecasting accuracy.
  • It has no government approval or certification of any kind.
  • Security testing so far is a developer self-assessment by the development assistant, not an independent audit or penetration test.
  • Telugu and Hindi text is machine-drafted and awaits native-speaker review; 1160 interface strings are listed as pending, and translated alert blocks are pending sign-off.
  • Linux and macOS start paths are written but have not been run there; all test results are from one Windows laptop.
  • Two live agencies and two real human approvers have not been tested; demo accounts do not establish real two-person approval.

Test evidence, all from the Windows laptop on 14 November 2026: API automated tests 1379 passed and 30 skipped; web Node tests 401 passed with the type check clean; security smoke script PASS; demo readiness GO; a backup-and-restore check passed; 496 page loads and 1310 clicks across six roles with no page error. These were run by the development assistant, not an independent party.

Versions

Version history

0.3.0 is the first tagged release. The product's package file said 0.2.0 from the first commit and no tag was ever created, so 0.2.0 and 0.1.0 are summaries of earlier work with a period instead of a release date. They have no tag. The entries follow the repository's own release notes and CHANGELOG.md.

0.3.0 14 November 2026, the first tagged release

  • Guided tours (a Welcome tour and one tour per page and tab, following your role) and a What's new page with release notes.
  • The Resilient Sensor Link rehearsal page with its storm timeline, and the patent credit (Indian Patent No. 598835).
  • A round of security and defect fixes found in testing: an origin check on one web route, platform-wide administration limited to the exercise agency's administrator, defensive API headers, escaping of three public-feed values, stricter request models, and a sign-out repair.
  • Walkthrough screenshots and videos re-recorded with the IndTrana name.

0.2.0 Summary of earlier work (no tagged release), up to 13 November 2026

  • The product became IndTrana, with sign-in for every page and data route, administrator brand settings, department and team accounts, and one-step install for Windows, macOS and Linux. Everything is still a local exercise on synthetic data.
  • Team response loop (rehearsal inside the app), opt-in email notices to IndTrana's own staff behind two switches, and communication channels on the Connectors page for credentials only.

0.1.0 Summary of earlier work (no tagged release), October 2026

  • The first local synthetic demonstration of the alert path, from evidence to an approved exercise draft.
  • Incident registry and workspace, source freshness and DataFusion replay, proposals with independent two-person approval, an approved-only alert draft, exercise tasks for departments, and a model evaluation lab that states its figures are not real forecasting accuracy.

Glossary

Terms used

Agency
An organisation using IndTrana. Every record belongs to one agency, and a person sees only their agency's records.
API
Application programming interface: the server program that holds the rules and talks to the database.
Audit trail
The permanent record of who did what, when and why.
Backend for the browser (BFF)
The server layer of the web application that keeps tokens and sessions so the browser never holds them.
CAP
Common Alerting Protocol: the standard format for an alert message. IndTrana only produces a private Draft CAP file marked Exercise.
Checker
The person who approves or rejects a proposal drafted by someone else.
Content Security Policy (CSP)
A browser rule that limits which scripts and connections a page may use.
Docker Compose
A tool that starts several programs (containers) together on one computer.
Exercise
A rehearsal on synthetic data. Nothing in an exercise is real or sent.
Identity provider
The agency's sign-in service. It holds passwords and second factors and issues signed statements of who a person is.
Kill switch
An administrator control that stops automated watch and scheduling at once.
Maker
The person who drafts and submits a proposal.
Maker-checker
A rule that two different people must draft and approve a consequential step.
OIDC
OpenID Connect: a standard way for an application to ask an identity provider who a person is.
PKCE
A protection that stops a stolen sign-in code being reused by someone else.
PostGIS
A PostgreSQL extension for maps and locations.
Proposal
A drafted action (for example a warning draft) with evidence, waiting for independent review.
Row-level security
A database feature that limits which rows a database account can read. Not yet built here.
Synthetic data
Invented data that looks like real data but describes no real event.
Token
A signed digital statement of identity, agency and role. In IndTrana it stays on the server.
Trust boundary
A line across which data must be checked again because the other side is not fully trusted.
IndTrana v0.3.0 · 14 November 2026 · Exercise prototype, synthetic data, not a live warning system. No government emblem, approval or endorsement.
